reader.requirement: At --std 85 the leftmost character position of every print line of a report is column number 1, so a COLUMN NUMBER IS integer-1 entry places the printable item's leftmost character at the integer-1-th position of the line (column 1 is the first byte, with no offset or prefix); the 1985 clause has only the absolute integer form, which must be nonzero.

edition-consulted.switches: only the citation text of the COLUMN 0 refusal (§1985:III.2 vs §2023:5.5); both editions refuse integer 0
the 2002 COLUMN forms (PLUS, LEFT/CENTER/RIGHT, multiple operands) are refused at 85 with COBOL0900; accepted at 2002+
bakes Edition into CobolReport; Place and NewLine never read it

reader.edition-search: grep DialectLevel|Edition|CobolVersion|IsActive in ReportWriterEmitter.cs, ReportModel.cs (ReportColumnSpec) and ReportWriter.cs Place/NewLine/ReportLineImage: the placement path (column-1 -> zero-based index in Place) consults no edition; only the grammar/construct gate for 2002 forms and the integer-operand message do.
reader.behaviour-differs-by-edition: no: column 1 is the first position at every edition; 85 only refuses the 2002 relative/aligned/multiple forms of the clause
reader.witnesses-cover: part: g85_z01 places items at columns 3 and 8 only; column 1 itself, adjacent items ending/starting on contiguous columns, a 19-character signed item and the COLUMN 0 degenerate form are not exercised

probes.printed: error COBOL2386: COLUMN 0: the integer operand 0 shall be nonzero — §1985:III.2
probes.expected: refused: there is no column 0 (GR4) and an integer must be nonzero (§1985:III.2)

probes.printed: error COBOL0900 x2: relative (PLUS) COLUMN operand / RIGHT alignment word requires COBOL-2002
probes.expected: refused at 85: the 1985 format is COLUMN NUMBER IS integer-1 only

citations.check: OK  §1985:XIII.3.11.4 GR4  (3.11.4 General Rules)  the text is in GR4

reader.notes: CobolReport.Place maps column n to zero-based index n-1 over a space-filled line image, and the 85 single-absolute-operand shape emits one Place call with integer-1 unchanged (AbsoluteLeftmost returns Value for the default LEFT alignment). The probe read the report file back byte by byte and every item sits at its 1-based column.

refuter.evidence: Attack: the 1985 CODE clause puts literal-1 in the first two positions of each report record and those positions are not part of the print line, so column 1 must be record byte 3. Probe refute-1985-222/code1.cob (two reports on one file, CODE "AB"/"CD", COLUMN 1 and 3) at --std 85 wrote 'ABX Y' and 'CDQQ' (od -c): column 1 sits after the code. Probe col3.cob: COLUMN 1 PIC X(5) JUSTIFIED RIGHT under a format-2 LINE entry printed '   AB' in 1-5, GROUP INDICATE at 6 only on the first detail, BLANK WHEN ZERO 7-9 blank, '|' at 10. Reader's col0/colplus cover the refusal and 2002-form halves. cite.py: OK §1985:XIII.3.11.4 GR4 'The leftmost position of the print line is considered to be column number 1'; OK §1985:XIII.3.6.4 GR1 'literal-1 is automatically placed in the first two character positions'; OK §1985:XIII.3.6.4 GR2 'are not included in the description of the print line'.
